description: Rename a set of files (any kind) with one pattern made of text and tokens: {name} the current name, {n} a number counting up ({n:3} for 001), {date} the file’s date as 2026-10-02, {w}x{h} the image size in pixels, {ext} the extension. The extension is always kept at the end. Starts with mode "preview", which only lists old → new and changes nothing; "copy" makes renamed copies in a new folder; "rename" renames in place.

digits.description: Digits in {n}: 0 adds zeros only as needed (01–12) so files sort in order. {n:3} in the pattern sets it there.

files.description: Files or folders (a folder means the files in it, not subfolders or hidden files), in the order to number them. ~ is your home folder.

letters.description: "keep": as typed; "lower": lower case; "web": lower case, dashes for spaces and only letters, numbers, dashes and dots.

mode.description: "preview": list the new names, change nothing. "copy": renamed copies in output_dir (default: a new folder named renamed next to the first file). "rename": rename the files where they are; refused if any new name is already taken.

output_dir.description: For mode "copy": the folder for the renamed copies.

pattern.description: The new name without the extension, e.g. "holiday-{n}" or "{date}-{name}".

start.description: The first number, e.g. 51 to carry on from a previous batch.

name: rename_files
title: Rename files
